sources.sample_test: C1000-179_SAM_SampleTestQiskitv2.pdf, same channel, sha256 8d191ff0be9dcdf4d5e03c8f8bb1e613b7e21a2bb5f5fb6bc79eb2d816c8989c — analyzed locally, NOT committed; 21 questions
sources.note: Both PDFs are public. This audit stores topic labels and statistics only — no official question text.

syllabus_fidelity.exam_facts: 68 questions / 90 min / pass 47 — verified from the rendered exam page 2026-07-26
objective_wording_fixes_applied: s4o1 -> official task 4.1 wording (execution modes: session with dedicated, priority, and batch mode)
s4o2 -> official task 4.2 wording (real hardware + broadcasting rules)
s5o1 -> 'such as dynamical decoupling' (official; also technically correct — SamplerV2 has no resilience_level)
s8o2 -> 'Interpret OpenQASM semantics' (dropped non-official 'for versions 2 and 3')
known_cosmetic_deltas: s3 objective order differs from official task order (ids stable; content 1:1)
s5o2 'Bypass runtime error mitigations' is an Advocate-Guide extra with no official TASK; folds under official 5.1 (annotated in syllabus.json)

anti_duplication.method: token-Jaccard, sample stem+options vs each bank question stem+code+options, stopworded
anti_duplication.verdict: PASS — no near-duplicates; top pairs manually reviewed (topical neighbors only)

study_guide_tasks.label: Define Pauli Operators
study_guide_tasks.reference_topics_covered: yes|Pauli labels/right-to-left ordering, phase prefixes, tensor vs expand, dot vs compose, to_matrix, commutation and SparsePauliOp are all exercised.
study_guide_tasks.note: 12 questions + 1 primer + 8 facts; direct hit on the sample-test Pauli-to_matrix item shape.

study_guide_tasks.label: Apply quantum operations
study_guide_tasks.reference_topics_covered: partial|Gate action, phases, Statevector/Operator and measurement probabilities are deep, but the circuit_library reference page (QFT, RealAmplitudes, EfficientSU2, TwoLocal/n_local, QuantumVolume, MCXGate, random_circuit) has ZERO questions and ZERO cram facts.
study_guide_tasks.note: 28 questions + 1 primer + 14 facts, but all on standard 1-2 qubit gates; the parameterized/algorithmic circuit library is absent even though it is one of only two references for this TASK.

study_guide_tasks.label: Visualize quantum circuits
study_guide_tasks.reference_topics_covered: yes|draw() output modes (text/mpl/latex), circuit_drawer function, style/idle_wires/reverse_bits/initial_state, mpl-figure return types.
study_guide_tasks.note: 9 questions + 1 primer + 9 facts.

study_guide_tasks.label: Visualize quantum measurements
study_guide_tasks.reference_topics_covered: partial|plot_histogram is well covered (6 items: number_to_keep, sort order, legend/overlay, DataBin->counts). plot_gate_map has ZERO hits anywhere in the repo (nor plot_error_map / plot_coupling_map / plot_circuit_layout). Rendering of a classical-feedforward circuit is touched by only one construction-flavoured item (s2-q013).
study_guide_tasks.note: 7 questions + 1 primer + 8 facts. An explicitly-referenced API (plot_gate_map) is entirely uncovered.

study_guide_tasks.label: Visualize quantum states
study_guide_tasks.reference_topics_covered: yes|plot_bloch_multivector 6 items (sphere count, axis/arrow, Bell-state reduced states, input types), plot_state_qsphere 3 items (node placement, colour=phase, draw_qsphere method).
study_guide_tasks.note: 10 questions + 1 primer + 9 facts.

study_guide_tasks.label: Construct dynamic circuits
study_guide_tasks.reference_topics_covered: yes|if_test/else_, switch/case, for_loop, mid-circuit measurement, removal of c_if in 2.x, when a dynamic circuit is genuinely required.
study_guide_tasks.note: 9 questions + 1 primer + 8 facts. NOTE our objective numbering is s3o2 while the official TASK number is 3.1.

study_guide_tasks.label: Construct parameterized circuits
study_guide_tasks.reference_topics_covered: partial|Parameter, ParameterVector, assign_parameters (list/dict/partial binding), immutability of the original circuit and parameter-order rules are covered. ParameterExpression appears in exactly ONE question (s3-q021, and only as a distractor label); arithmetic on expressions is tested behaviourally but the class API (bind, subs, is_real, gradient, sympify) is not.
study_guide_tasks.note: 9 questions + 1 primer + 9 facts; matches sample-test item 7 exactly (Parameter vs ParameterExpression vs string).

study_guide_tasks.label: Transpile and optimize circuits
study_guide_tasks.reference_topics_covered: partial|generate_preset_pass_manager, optimization levels 0-3, StagedPassManager stage names, layout/routing/translation/scheduling behaviour and ISA reasoning are strong. The transpiler_passes API page is nearly untouched: only TrivialLayout and CommutativeCancellation are ever named (1 mention each); SabreLayout/SabreSwap/VF2Layout/VF2PostLayout/BasisTranslator/UnitarySynthesis/Collect2qBlocks/ConsolidateBlocks/ElidePermutations/HighLevelSynthesis/PadDynamicalDecoupling never appear.
study_guide_tasks.note: 15 questions + 1 primer + 13 facts; stage-level coverage good, pass-class-level coverage thin.

study_guide_tasks.label: Construct basic quantum circuits
study_guide_tasks.reference_topics_covered: yes|QuantumRegister/ClassicalRegister, compose vs append (in-place trap), measure/measure_all with explicit bit mapping, depth/size/width, register naming.
study_guide_tasks.note: 11 questions + 1 primer + 9 facts; covers sample-test item 8 (which register stores a measurement).

study_guide_tasks.label: Demonstrate an understanding of execution modes (session with dedicated/priority, batch)
study_guide_tasks.reference_topics_covered: yes|job/session/batch selection, dedicated vs priority language, interactive vs max TTL, session close semantics, Open Plan restrictions, when batch does NOT help.
study_guide_tasks.note: 20 questions + 1 primer + 12 facts. Strongest-covered TASK relative to weight.

study_guide_tasks.label: Run circuits on real hardware with Runtime primitives, applying broadcasting rules
study_guide_tasks.reference_topics_covered: partial|Primitives/ISA requirement, QiskitRuntimeService, least_busy, mode= argument, PUB submission and job/result plumbing are covered. Broadcasting is covered MECHANICALLY (shapes, sweep counts: s5-q016/017/023/035/039, s6-q023/024/025) but the docs' NAMED broadcasting patterns and their diagrams -- exactly what sample item 12 asks -- are never named anywhere in the bank or cram.
study_guide_tasks.note: 19 questions (+ ~7 broadcasting items filed under s5/s6) + 2 primers + 11 facts.

study_guide_tasks.label: Set sampler primitive options such as dynamical decoupling
study_guide_tasks.reference_topics_covered: yes|dynamical_decoupling.enable/sequence_type, twirling group fields (12 questions mention twirling), default_shots, seed_simulator, the 'Sampler has no resilience_level' trap, and manual/custom mitigation when bypassing runtime defaults.
study_guide_tasks.note: 14 questions (9 on s5o1 + 5 on s5o2) + 2 primers + 15 facts. NOTE our s5o2 ('Bypass runtime error mitigations and implement your own') has NO counterpart TASK in the official study guide; it folds under 5.1.

study_guide_tasks.label: Understand the theoretical background behind the sampler primitive
study_guide_tasks.reference_topics_covered: yes|run([pub]) call shape, per-shot BitArray semantics, DataBin/register naming, PUB shapes and broadcasting, shots accounting, V1->V2 migration traps (s4-q016).
study_guide_tasks.note: 18 questions + 1 primer + 16 facts.

study_guide_tasks.label: Set estimator primitive options (such as resilience levels)
study_guide_tasks.reference_topics_covered: yes|resilience_level 0/1/2 validation and defaults, resilience.zne_mitigation vs resilience.zne.{amplifier,noise_factors,extrapolator}, pec_mitigation, measure_mitigation/TREX, twirling group, dynamical_decoupling; cram primer enumerates the full nested option tree with documented defaults.
study_guide_tasks.note: 13 questions + 2 primers + 13 facts. Best cram-to-API alignment in the bank.

study_guide_tasks.label: Understand the theoretical background behind the estimator primitive
study_guide_tasks.reference_topics_covered: yes|PUB tuple (circuit, observables, parameter_values, precision), precision<->shots quadratic law, SparsePauliOp construction, apply_layout, observable arrays/broadcasting, evs/stds result access, suppression vs mitigation split.
study_guide_tasks.note: 20 questions + 2 primers + 19 facts; covers sample items 15 and 17 head-on.

study_guide_tasks.label: Retrieve previous experiment results (session/Qiskit Runtime)
study_guide_tasks.reference_topics_covered: partial|service.job(job_id)/service.jobs(), job.result(), PrimitiveResult/PubResult indexing, DataBin/BitArray access, get_counts, register-name traps and result serialization are all covered. The two class names in the references are near-absent as such: SamplerPubResult appears twice and only as DISTRACTOR text (s5-q011 F, s5-q039 B); BasePrimitiveJob appears ZERO times (its method surface -- result/status/cancel/job_id/done/in_final_state -- is nevertheless exercised).
study_guide_tasks.note: 21 questions + 3 primers + 21 facts; behavioural coverage is strong, class-name recognition is the soft spot.

study_guide_tasks.label: Monitor jobs
study_guide_tasks.reference_topics_covered: partial|session.details() is covered exactly once (s7-q030) and JobStatus exactly once (s7-q033, where it is the correct answer). The qiskit.providers module page (BackendV2, JobV1/JobStatus enum members QUEUED/RUNNING/DONE/CANCELLED/ERROR, provider interface) is otherwise untested; job.cancel is covered by s7-q028.
study_guide_tasks.note: only 4 questions + 2 primers + 8 facts for a TASK that is half of a 10%-weight section AND supplies one of the 21 sample items.

study_guide_tasks.label: Structure types in OpenQASM 3 programs
study_guide_tasks.reference_topics_covered: partial|s8-q022 (multi) reads the feature table across int[n]/bit[n]/angle/complex/const/duration/stretch, and s8-q016/q020 cover emitted bit[]/int[]/float declarations. The openqasm.com types page itself -- type widths, implicit vs explicit casting rules, bool/uint/float/angle/complex casting, arrays -- is not tested anywhere.
study_guide_tasks.note: 3 questions + 1 primer + 3 facts, and only one of the three is genuinely about the OpenQASM 3 type system. Sample item 20 lands squarely here.

study_guide_tasks.label: Interpret OpenQASM semantics
study_guide_tasks.reference_topics_covered: yes|qasm3 vs qasm2 register declarations (qubit[]/bit[] vs qreg/creg), include files (stdgates.inc vs qelib1.inc), control-flow support differences, version-string semantics.
study_guide_tasks.note: 4 questions tagged s8o2 (+4 more s8o3 items that carry the same semantics) + 1 primer + 4 facts.

study_guide_tasks.label: Interoperate different versions of OpenQASM with Qiskit
study_guide_tasks.reference_topics_covered: yes|dumps/dump/loads/load for both qasm2 and qasm3, file-stream export, the qiskit-qasm3-import optional-dependency asymmetry, round-trip of global phase, custom gates, unbound Parameters.
study_guide_tasks.note: 10 questions + 1 primer + 4 facts; covers sample item 21 exactly.

study_guide_tasks.label: Interact with the Qiskit IBM Runtime REST API
study_guide_tasks.reference_topics_covered: partial|Bearer/IAM auth header, POST /jobs submission with a QASM/PUB payload and required program_id/backend fields, and token-scope behaviour are covered at a conceptual level. Endpoint inventory (GET /jobs/{id}/results, /backends, /sessions, /instances), response codes and pagination are not.
study_guide_tasks.note: only 3 questions + 1 primer + 3 facts for a full official TASK; smallest per-TASK coverage in the bank.

sample_test_topics.note: Direct analogue: our items ask the same label-ordering / to_matrix question in both directions, incl. a spot-bug on ZI vs IZ.
s1-q022 is T applied to |1> asked as a statevector; s1-q028 is the same shape for p(pi/2); s1-q027 covers QuantumCircuit.global_phase explicitly.
s1-q039 is RY(pi/3) -> P(1); same computation, different angle. Note none of ours uses the exact ry(pi/2) -> 0.5 case.

We test how to BUILD the conditional (s2-q013) and what it OUTPUTS (s3-q026), but never how a classical-feedforward block RENDERS. The official reference for TASK 2.2 is the classical-feedforward guide, so this framing is deliberate on IBM's side.
Histogram semantics well covered. Two sub-gaps: Statevector.sample_counts / sample_memory appear ZERO times in the repo, and we never ask 'which figure is produced' with image options.

sample_test_topics.topic: Identify the circuit behind a q-sphere figure
sample_test_topics.note: We cover q-sphere node placement and phase colouring, but never reverse-engineer a circuit from a figure; only 3 q-sphere items total.

sample_test_topics.topic: Parameter vs ParameterExpression for an unbound angle
sample_test_topics.note: s3-q021 has the ParameterExpression-wrapper misconception as an explicit distractor (option F), which is precisely the official item's distractor d.
Recall-level item; ours are harder (bit-mapping and CircuitError variants) but the fact is covered.

sample_test_topics.topic: Output circuit of generate_preset_pass_manager with coupling_map/initial_layout
sample_test_topics.note: s3-q043 is initial_layout on a 5-qubit backend; s3-q032/041 are routing on a line. Ours ask for gate counts/ISA facts rather than 'which drawn circuit'.

sample_test_topics.topic: Which three are Qiskit Runtime execution modes
sample_test_topics.note: s4-q039 is a 'Which THREE' multi item on execution modes -- structurally identical.

sample_test_topics.topic: Correct way to open a Session
sample_test_topics.note: s4-q028 is the same 'which snippet correctly opens a session and runs' shape.

sample_test_topics.topic: Name the array-broadcasting pattern shown in a diagram
sample_test_topics.note: Broadcasting MECHANICS are covered well (7 items on shapes and execution counts) but the docs' NAMED patterns / diagram-recognition framing is absent: 'all-to-all', 'standard multidimensional array generalization' etc. never occur in a broadcasting sense anywhere in the bank.
s5-q026 is default_shots vs per-PUB shots precedence; s5-q033 is the setter. Definitional framing ('number of times we run the circuit') is implicit rather than asked directly.
s5-q001 and s5-q013 are the same 'which call shape is valid' item, incl. the bare-circuit-not-in-a-list error.

sample_test_topics.topic: Effect on shots of loosening Estimator precision
sample_test_topics.note: s6-q017 is the tighten-precision direction of the identical question; s6-q038 is a multi on the precision<->shots law.

sample_test_topics.topic: Which mitigation is available via resilience options (ZNE)
sample_test_topics.note: s6-q019 is the exact 'which of these are mitigation (not suppression)' discrimination, incl. the DD and Pauli-twirling distractors.
s6-q025 is a spot-bug on exactly the (circuit, observable, parameter_values, precision) slot order.

sample_test_topics.topic: Purpose of a Qiskit Runtime session
sample_test_topics.note: Content covered, but ALL of it is filed under our section 4. IBM places this conceptual item in exam Section 7 -- a cross-section placement mismatch that would distort mock-exam stratification.
Exactly one covering item (s7-q030, a multi listing state / last-job timestamps / mode). Single point of failure for a topic that IBM chose to put in a 21-question sample.

Only s8-q022 touches the type inventory, and it does so through the Qiskit feature table rather than the OpenQASM 3 type system itself. No item asks 'which of these is a valid OpenQASM 3 classical type'.

sample_test_topics.topic: Export a circuit to OpenQASM 3 into a file stream
sample_test_topics.note: s8-q011 is dump-to-open-file-object vs dumps-to-string -- the same discrimination as the official item.

gaps.suggestion: ZERO occurrences across 243 questions and 216 cram facts, yet it is one of three explicit references for TASK 2.2. Add 2-3 items: what plot_gate_map takes as input (a BackendV2 / coupling map), what it renders (qubit connectivity, not results), and plot_gate_map vs plot_error_map vs plot_circuit_layout.

ZERO hits for QFT/QFTGate, RealAmplitudes, EfficientSU2, TwoLocal, n_local, QuantumVolume, MCXGate, random_circuit. One of only two references for TASK 1.2 (16%-weight section). Add 2-3 items on constructing a library circuit and on its parameter count.

4 questions / 8 facts total for s7o2; JobStatus appears in exactly 1 question and session.details() in exactly 1. Add items on JobStatus enum members and terminal vs non-terminal states, and a second session.details() item so sample-item-19 coverage is not a single point of failure.

Shape mechanics are covered by 7 items, but the named patterns IBM asks about ('all-to-all', 'standard multidimensional array generalization', SU2-style diagrams) never appear. Add 1-2 items that name the pattern given a parameter/observable array pairing.

gaps.topic: OpenQASM 3 type system and casting rules
gaps.suggestion: s8o1 has 3 questions / 3 facts, and only s8-q022 is really about types -- via the Qiskit feature table, not openqasm.com. Add a 'which is a valid OpenQASM 3 classical type' item (complex/uint/angle/bool/duration/stretch vs char/class/enum) and one on implicit vs explicit casting.

gaps.topic: Qiskit Runtime REST API endpoint surface
gaps.suggestion: 3 questions / 3 facts. Auth and job POST are covered; result retrieval, backend/session/instance endpoints and response handling are not. Add 1-2 items.

Only TrivialLayout and CommutativeCancellation are ever named. Stage-level coverage is strong, so this is a recall-level top-up: add 1-2 items mapping pass classes (SabreLayout/SabreSwap, VF2Layout, BasisTranslator, ConsolidateBlocks) to their stage.

Behaviour is thoroughly covered but the two referenced class names appear 2x (distractor-only) and 0x respectively. Add one item that names SamplerPubResult as the per-PUB result type and one on the BasePrimitiveJob method surface.

Expressions are tested behaviourally (s3-q021) but ParameterExpression is named only once, as a distractor. IBM lists it as a top-level reference for TASK 3.2; add one item on when a Parameter becomes a ParameterExpression.
ZERO occurrences in the repo; the official item builds its histogram from state.sample_counts(shots=1024). Add one item that samples counts from a Statevector.

4 of 21 official items (19%) present IMAGES as options. Our bank has zero image-bearing items -- an entire question FORMAT of the real exam is unrehearsed. Either add rendered-figure items or add an explicit 'read the ASCII/text drawing' surrogate.

IBM asks 'what is the purpose of a Runtime session' inside exam Section 7 (10% weight); all six of our covering items sit in section s4. Mock-exam stratification by section will under-fill s7 and over-fill s4 relative to the real blueprint.

gaps.topic: syllabus.json resource list is guide-weighted; the official guide is API-weighted
gaps.suggestion: 25 of 43 official reference URLs are /api/ pages; 28 of 43 official URLs are absent from syllabus.json resources, including every options-*-options page, runtime-job, session, providers, JobStatus, SamplerPubResult, BasePrimitiveJob, transpiler_passes, circuit, circuit_library, Parameter, ParameterExpression, plot_gate_map, plot_bloch_multivector, plot_state_qsphere, qasm3, qiskit-runtime-rest, get-started-with-primitives and migration-guides/v2-primitives. Question explanations already cite 16 distinct API pages, so this is a syllabus-metadata lag, not a content lag.

gaps.topic: syllabus.json records guides/execute-on-hardware as a non-existent slug
gaps.suggestion: syllabus.json s4.resource_gaps says "'Execute on hardware' guide name has no exact slug", but the official study guide references https://quantum.cloud.ibm.com/docs/en/guides/execute-on-hardware verbatim under BOTH TASK 4.1 and 4.2. The slug exists; remove the resource_gap note and add the URL.
Section task counts are 2/3/4/2/2/2/2/4 = 21. Any downstream artefact assuming 17 TASKs is wrong.

gaps.topic: Our objective s5o2 has no official TASK
gaps.suggestion: The official Section 5 has exactly two TASKs (5.1 options incl. dynamical decoupling, 5.2 theory). Our s5o2 'Bypass runtime error mitigations and implement your own' (5 questions, 1 primer, 6 facts) is unmapped; it is defensible content but should be shown as folded into 5.1, and note that official 5.1 is worded 'such as dynamical decoupling' where our s5o1 says 'such as resilience levels' -- the Sampler has no resilience_level, so IBM's wording is the safer one.

gaps.topic: Section 3 objective ORDER differs from official
gaps.suggestion: Official 3.1 dynamic / 3.2 parameterized / 3.3 transpile / 3.4 basic; ours s3o1 basic / s3o2 dynamic / s3o3 parameterized / s3o4 transpile. Content maps 1:1 but any UI that shows 'objective 3.1' will mislabel.

sample_test.difficulty_judgment: Predominantly recall / single-step application. ~9 of 21 are pure recall (2,8,10,13,16,17,18,19,20,21-ish), ~8 require one evaluation step, and only 12 (broadcast-pattern naming) and 6/9 (figure recognition) demand real synthesis.

deviations: Stem-code share 76.1% vs sample 57.1% (33.3% if only stem code blocks count) -- our bank is markedly more code-heavy. Recommendation: keep, but ensure each section retains a few prose-only recall items (s1 currently has 0 of 37 without code).
Multi-select share 11.9% vs sample 9.5% -- well matched; no change needed.

Authored option counts are 6 (194) or 5 (48); the sample test uses 4 options for 19 of 21 items. Displayed counts (4 for 178, 5 for 61) land the bank in the right place, so this is a display-layer success. Recommendation: raise the share of display_count=4 for single-answer items and reserve 5-6 for multi.
4 multi items carry display_count=null (s2-q031, s3-q042, s6-q028, s7-q030) and will fall back to whatever the renderer defaults to. Recommendation: set display_count explicitly on all four.
One item authored with only 4 options (s2-q031) has no room for display rotation. Recommendation: extend its pool to 5-6.

Stem length: sample median 14 words (mean 16.9, range 10-28) vs ours median 23 (mean 23.7, range 4-59) -- our stems are ~64% longer because they carry scenario framing the official items omit. Recommendation: no functional change needed, but trim the longest 10% (stems above ~45 words) so timing practice stays realistic at 79 s/question. Code blocks: sample median 5 lines (range 4-14) vs ours median 6 (range 1-15) -- matched.
Output-prediction share 32.1% (78 of 243) vs 33.3% of the sample -- an excellent match, and the single strongest style alignment in the bank.

ZERO image-bearing items vs 19% of the sample test (4 of 21: draw(mpl) output, histogram figure, q-sphere figure, broadcasting diagram). This is the largest format divergence. Recommendation: add a small set of figure-recognition items (rendered PNG/SVG options, or text-drawing surrogates for circuit rendering).

Difficulty skews harder than the sample: 48 of 243 (19.8%) are difficulty 3 and only 69 (28.4%) are difficulty 1, whereas roughly 40-45% of the sample items are pure recall. Recommendation: this is defensible for a prep bank, but the timed mock-exam sampler should over-weight difficulty 1-2 so a 68-item mock feels like the real 90-minute paper.
Answer-key balance is good across A-D (74/74/72/61) with E/F rare (10/3), consistent with display_count 4-5 rotation. No action.

Section volumes track weights loosely: s3 44 items / 18% weight and s8 16 items / 6% weight are proportionate, but s7 has 24 items for a 10% weight while s2 has 26 for 11%; s4 (36 items, 15%) is over-served relative to s7. Recommendation: the s7o2 shortfall (4 items) is the real imbalance to fix.
